title: Interlocks and permissives
summary: Interlocks prevent dangerous or damaging combinations: a pump must not run on an empty tank, two contactors must not close together, a valve must be open before a pump starts.

sections.heading: Permissive versus trip
sections.body:
- A **permissive** is a condition required to **start** (for example: tank level above low-low).
- A **trip** stops equipment that is already running when a condition is lost (for example: overload relay opened).
Many interlocks are both: they block a start and stop a running device.

sections.heading: Writing interlocks
Safety is separate
sections.body: Standard PLC interlocks protect equipment and product. Protection of people is the job of a **safety system** (safety relays or safety PLCs designed to the relevant standards). PLC Lab does not model safety controllers.
